_comment: STARTER SKETCH — nothing reads this yet. Role/economics annotations for
the mons whose value the leaf eval structurally cannot price.
WHY A DATA FILE AND NOT AN LLM CALL. The knowledge here is ENUMERABLE (a
few dozen meta mons, each with a stable role), so it belongs in a
versioned, diffable artifact with zero inference latency — the same call
made for ps_sets_overrides.json, where a 40-line overlay fixed the
Kingambit Low Kick blindness that would otherwise have needed a model.
An LLM+RAG pass over the smogon corpus is a good way to DRAFT this file
(Phase 0 of the overlay plan) but the artifact is the deliverable, and it
must be human-reviewed before anything consumes it. Contextual judgements
that cannot be enumerated ('is THIS Kingambit worth holding on THIS board')
stay with the search or a later live overlay.
WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL. Three open items are each blocked on the same
missing fact — which mons are cleaners, which are resource anchors, which
are meant to lead:
1. Kingambit hold-back annuity: the eval now prices Supreme Overlord's
fallen-ally scaling (poke-engine c68f15a) but still cannot see the
OPPORTUNITY COST of spending the cleaner early; it needs to know the
mon is a cleaner at all.
2. Weather preservation: measured 43% rain uptime with 41% of Swift Swim
moves clicked OUTSIDE rain — the search does not treat the setter's
survival as a resource, or the weather clock as a wasting asset.
3. Canonical-lead weighting: the preview matrix is nearly flat (row-min
spreads 0.01-0.12 at any depth) so lead choice is close to a coin
flip among near-ties; paste slot-1 and role are real human priors.
SAFETY CONTRACT: every consumer must degrade to current behaviour on a
missing entry. This file may only ADD information; it must never be
required. Absent species = today's engine, unchanged.
SCHEMA (per normalized species; `ability` qualifies when the role depends
on it, since the same species with another ability is a different mon):
tags         role labels, the primary key for consumers
ability      role holds only for this ability (omit = any)
value_curve  how worth changes over a game: flat | grows_with_own_faints
| decays_with_weather_clock | grows_with_hazards
preserve     how badly losing it costs beyond its own HP: low|med|high
resource     field state this mon CREATES; its death ends it
requires     field state this mon NEEDS to be worth its slot
entry_condition  precondition for this mon's PLAN, not its survival: e.g.
full_hp when a Sash/Multiscale sequence needs a clean
entry. Distinct from preserve (cost of losing it) and
requires (a field state). Added 2026-07-31 after the
Ceruledge entry needed a concept neither field had.
lead_intent  human intent to lead it: avoid | neutral | strong
conditional   list of {when, ...overrides}: role/value that only exists
`when` vocabulary is of TWO kinds and they are not
interchangeable: TEAM-COMPOSITION (opponent_has:<tag>,
opponent_lacks:<tag>) is knowable at team preview, while
BOARD-STATE (board:hazards_up, board:weather_up) is only true
at some moments of a game. Spinblocking is the type case: the
Ghost typing blocks Rapid Spin ALWAYS, but it is worth nothing
until hazards are actually standing that the other side wants
to clear — so the tag is unconditional and the VALUE is
board-gated.
axis          which side of the split a role operates on — {attacks: ...}
and, for anything tagged wall, {defends: ...}. Values:
physical | special | mixed. A wall is only a wall against one
side, and a sweeper only threatens through one stat, so a bare
'wall' or 'setup-sweeper' tag leaves out the thing that decides
whether it checks the mon in front of it. Set per-set where a
species splits: Kyurem's Choice Specs set attacks specially
while its Dragon Dance set attacks physically.
sets          for species that genuinely split into different Pokemon
Each set may carry `prevalence`: roughly what fraction of that
species' sets run it, estimated as the signature move's usage
divided by 25% (a set holds four moves, so any one move tops
Three signature kinds, in order of preference: a MOVE unique to
the set (usage / 25%), else the ITEM (usage directly — one item
Ability is often ORTHOGONAL to the set rather than a set of its
own — a Choice Specs Dragapult may run either Infiltrator or
Clear Body — so an ability split is recorded at species level in
`ability_split` and mentioned in the fact, not modelled as a
Some sets have NO positive signature — an all-out-attacker build
is defined by what it lacks, and a form item like Wellspring Mask
is on every set. Those get a RESIDUAL estimate (whatever the
signature-derived sets leave over) with prevalence_method set to
'residual' so a reader can weight it accordingly: it absorbs the
combined error of the others and assumes the sets partition
cleanly. An estimate beats a blank — but label how it was made.
which would quietly absorb every estimation error in the others.
identifies one build.
out near 25%). It is an ESTIMATE, not ground truth — shared
moves and four-move overlap blur it — but it separates a set
that is nearly universal from one that is fringe. Ceruledge
runs Swords Dance on ~84% of sets and Bulk Up on ~8%; listing
both without that weighting would be its own kind of
confidently-wrong, hedging into noise instead of calibrating.
depending on set. The top-level fact/tags hold what is true of
EVERY set (typing, ability); each entry here carries what is
true only of that one. A consumer should key off the inferred
set when it has one and fall back to the species otherwise.
against certain opposing teams. Static fields describe the
DEFAULT case; a matching `when` replaces them. Added
2026-07-31 — Magic Bounce Hatterene is a hazard-denial
anchor against a team with setters and close to dead weight
against one without, and a single `preserve` cannot say
both. `when` vocabulary: opponent_has:<tag>, opponent_lacks:<tag>.
deployment    HOW the mon is meant to be brought in, which the search
cannot infer from the board: lead | bait-switch | pivot-cycle
| late-cleaner | sacrifice. Distinct from lead_intent (which
only answers 'should it start the game'). bait-switch means
it is sent in to INVITE a specific opponent action and punish
it — Hatterene switching in on a predicted hazard turn to
bounce it is the type case, and it is explicitly NOT a lead.
Values: lead | bait-switch | pivot-cycle | late-cleaner |
sacrifice | setup-window (needs a FREE entry to begin a
multi-turn plan — Ceruledge and Multiscale Dragonite).
sequence      the ordered play a mon's value actually comes from, for the
cases where no single turn of it looks good. Added 2026-07-31
(user): Ceruledge's line deliberately TAKES a hit, so a search
scoring each turn on immediate safety declines the whole plan.
This is the beyond-horizon knowledge in its most explicit form
— write the chain down rather than hoping depth finds it.
fact          WHAT THE MON DOES, plainly. This is the only field a consumer
WHERE THE META IS GENUINELY SPREAD, SAY SO. Do not manufacture
a modal answer: Darkrai's items run Boots 21% / Specs 18% /
Scarf 16% / Life Orb 12% / Leftovers 11%, so 'usually Choice
Scarf' is a confident claim the data does not support. A
confidently wrong belief is worse than an honestly vague one —
the same lesson the opponent-belief work learned the hard way,
where sharper-but-wrong sets lost to calibrated spread. Prefer
'runs several sets' plus the `sets` list over inventing a
single answer.
should ever be shown: present tense, mechanically true, and
OPPONENT-AGNOSTIC. No campaign history, no commit hashes, no
named opponents — a note about how one specific ladder bot
builds its teams is per-opponent knowledge that belongs in the
scouting book, and feeding it here would mislead us against
everyone else. Narrative prose also invites a downstream model
to narrativise; plain facts do not.
provenance    HUMAN REVIEW ONLY, never shown to a consumer: where the claim
came from, what corrected what, citations and commits. Kept so
a reviewer can audit a fact without that history contaminating
the fact itself.
REVIEW RULE: an entry without `evidence` is a guess and should not ship.
Role tags are TESTABLE against behaviour — the Kingambit timing analysis
(first-entry turn, allies fallen at entry) is the template; a claimed
'cleaner' whose deployment timing does not move after wiring is a claim
that failed, not a fact.

kingambit.fact: Supreme Overlord raises its power by 10% for each fallen ally, so it is weakest at full team and strongest last. Sucker Punch gives it priority. Spending it early forfeits the scaling it exists for.
kingambit.provenance: Supreme Overlord = +10% power per fallen ally (abilities.rs:2257), now mirrored into threat_vs (c68f15a). Timing instrument: we first deploy it ~T9 with 0.44 allies down and 77% of the time with ZERO down, vs the ladder population's T13.0 / 0.96. fp is equally guilty, so this is absolute strength, not fp-gap.

pelipper.fact: Drizzle sets rain the moment it enters, and Damp Rock extends the duration. The rain ends early if another weather setter replaces it.
pelipper.provenance: rain_audit over 27 rain-team games: 43% average uptime where a piloted Damp Rock team lives 60-80%; uptime tracked outcomes (50% in wins vs 40% in losses). Rain teams benched at 29.2% board-only, the only below-pool-CI archetype.

barraskewda.fact: Swift Swim doubles its Speed in rain, so it outspeeds most of the field only while rain is up and is ordinary without it.
barraskewda.provenance: 41% of Swift Swim moves across those games were clicked OUTSIDE rain (60 in / 42 out) — the search spends the abuser while its enabling condition is down.

torkoal.fact: Drought sets sun on entry and Heat Rock extends it. Its own Speed is very low, so it exists to enable partners.
torkoal.provenance: same audit: sun leaks identically (43% uptime) but sun teams win anyway (63%) because Protosynthesis abusers fall back on Booster Energy — so preserve pressure is genuinely LOWER here than for rain. Recorded to stop a future fix over-generalising 'weather setter' into one rule.

glimmora.fact: Toxic Debris sets Toxic Spikes when it is hit by a physical move. Stealth Rock and Mortal Spin give it hazard control, and Focus Sash guarantees it gets at least one layer down.
glimmora.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Glimmora (gen9ou) — Lead]: the Lead set exists to deny setup — it stops "Ting-Lu from setting up entry hazards multiple times and Hatterene from trying to deny Stealth Rock with Magic Bounce". Confirms the suicide-lead role: its job is completed on the turns it survives, not by surviving. Directly relevant to richwoman, whose hazard stack is anchored by Ting-Lu (45 leads).

grimmsnarl.fact: Prankster gives its status moves priority, so it sets Reflect and Light Screen before being attacked. Light Clay extends both to eight turns.
grimmsnarl.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Grimmsnarl (gen9ou) — Dual Screens]: recommended set is Reflect / Light Screen / Taunt / Spirit Break with LIGHT CLAY, an item bought purely to extend the side conditions it leaves behind — the definition of expendable team-persistent support. Matches the monotype screens-setter precedent.

slowkinggalar.fact: Regenerator restores a third of its HP whenever it switches out, so repeated entries cost it almost nothing. Chilly Reception switches it out while setting snow, and Future Sight lands two turns later so it threatens even after leaving the field.
slowkinggalar.provenance: Regenerator pivots are net-positive on entry (fp routes hazard cycles through them: pays 12.5%, regains 33%) — the hazard_cycle finding. Also the mon whose speed floor produced the false Choice Scarf call (88f1f17), so its canonical spread is bulky with ~0 Speed. [Trimmed 2026-07-31: the fact had noted its low Speed investment, which was only interesting because of a speed-inference bug on our side — session detail, not a property a reader needs. Removed.]

sets.name: Assault Vest
sets.fact: Assault Vest adds special bulk at the cost of its status moves, so it checks attackers rather than pivoting.

sets.name: Defensive Pivot
sets.fact: Boots plus Regenerator and Chilly Reception make every switch nearly free.

conditional.note: The spinblock only cashes in when hazards are actually standing that the other side wants to clear. The typing blocks Rapid Spin regardless, but with an empty field or an opponent carrying no removal it changes nothing, and the mon is being kept for its attacking sets instead.

gholdengo.fact: Good as Gold makes it immune to status moves. Its Ghost typing blocks Rapid Spin, so hazards its side has set cannot be spun away while it is alive — this is true of every set, being a property of its typing rather than its moves. Air Balloon, its most common item, adds a temporary Ground immunity.
gholdengo.provenance: USER-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: my entry reduced a top-3 usage Pokemon to 'spinblocker', omitting that it is a primary win condition. Usage data confirms the correction — Shadow Ball 21.1% and Make It Rain 20.8% are its two most-used moves, Nasty Plot 12.8%, Recover 12.5%, Trick 8.4% (Choice Scarf is 33% of its items), Thunder Wave 4.1% with Hex 3.1%, Air Balloon 44% of items. Smogon's analysis calls it "both a defensive and offensive glue on virtually any team" and carries a dedicated Offensive Nasty Plot set. SCHEMA LIMITATION this exposed: the file annotates a SPECIES, but this mon has several sets with genuinely different roles (Nasty Plot sweeper, Choice Scarf Trick, defensive status/Hex). Tags and fact now cover all of them, which is lossy — a consumer cannot tell WHICH set is in front of it. The set-inference tiers already identify that at runtime, so a future consumer should key role off the inferred set rather than the species alone. Same class of gap as the sole-remover team-property problem. [Refined 2026-07-31 (user): spinblocking is a TYPING property so the tag is unconditional — what is conditional is whether it matters, which needs hazards actually on the field, not merely a hazard-setter on the roster. Split into per-set entries at the same time.]

sets.name: Nasty Plot
sets.fact: Nasty Plot doubles its Special Attack, then Shadow Ball and Make It Rain sweep. Recover sustains it across the game.
sequence: enter on a status move or an attack it absorbs — Good as Gold ignores status outright and Air Balloon dodges Ground moves until it is popped
Nasty Plot on that free turn, doubling Special Attack
attack with Shadow Ball, which is the repeatable one
use Make It Rain only as a finisher: it hits harder but lowers its own Special Attack, undoing the boost
Recover to reset if the sweep stalls and the free turn comes again
sets.sequence_note: The item choice decides the entry: Air Balloon buys a free switch-in against Ground moves but pops on any other hit, so the setup turn usually has to be taken before it is gone.

sets.name: Choice Scarf
sets.fact: A Choice Scarf makes it fast enough to revenge-kill, and Trick can pass that Scarf to a wall to cripple it.

sets.name: Status Hex
sets.fact: Thunder Wave or Will-O-Wisp inflicts status, then Hex doubles in power against the statused target.

gliscor.fact: Poison Heal turns being poisoned into recurring healing rather than damage, so it has to be statused before it does anything — the Toxic Orb it carries applies that poison at the end of a turn. Protect does two jobs: it blocks Knock Off, which matters because losing the orb disables Poison Heal outright, and it stalls turns while the healing ticks. Substitute blocks status and chip from behind.
gliscor.provenance: The flagship annuity case. Stall audit: fp's Poison Heal Gliscor played its FULL PP budget and generated 22.8 mons of free healing over three marathons while ours clicked 6 moves in ~711 turns. Eval terms shipped for exactly this (poke-engine 76af1e9: POISON_HEAL_STATUSED 15->35, PENDING +15) and our Gliscor now SubToxes at full budget. Known race: the naked orb walked into Knock Off on entry in 2/3 marathons, so activation timing is itself the play. [USER-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: the fact described Protect as only stalling for heal ticks. Its other job is blocking Knock Off to keep the Toxic Orb, without which the whole set does nothing.]

conditional.note: Hazard removal is only worth something while the opponent is setting hazards. Against a team that sets none, the removal move is a wasted slot.

greattusk.fact: Rapid Spin removes entry hazards for the whole team. Protosynthesis raises its Speed, letting it outpace threats that would normally be faster. Its removal is a service to teammates, not a personal benefit.
greattusk.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Great Tusk (gen9ou) — Offensive Utility / Defensive]: "Rapid Spin allows it to remove entry hazards for its teammates, and the Speed boost lets it scare out usually faster threats like Darkrai and Iron Crown"; also "a staple on Sticky Web teams". SOLE-REMOVER CAVEAT: preserve:high holds only when it is the team's only remover — a TEAM property this per-species file cannot express (schema gap). Hazard chip is our pinned loss mechanism (SR = 21% of damage taken), so the remover is a team-persistent resource. [SCHEMA GAP, reviewer note: preserve also depends on whether OUR OWN team carries another remover — a team property this per-species file cannot express, and `conditional` only covers opponent facts. Moved out of the consumer-facing note 2026-07-31.]

sets.name: Offensive Utility
sets.fact: Booster Energy raises a stat on entry, pairing immediate offence with Rapid Spin removal.

sets.name: Bulk Up
sets.fact: Bulk Up raises Attack and Defence together so it can boost while absorbing physical hits.

conditional.note: Hazard removal is only worth something while the opponent is setting hazards. Against a team that sets none, the removal move is a wasted slot.

corviknight.fact: Defog clears hazards from both sides. Pressure makes opponents spend two PP per move. Roost and high Defense let it re-enter repeatedly. About a fifth run Mirror Armor instead of Pressure, reflecting stat drops back at the attacker rather than taxing PP.
corviknight.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Corviknight (gen9ou) — Defensive]: "Defog allows Corviknight to fulfill the role as the team's hazard remover", and Pressure "more quickly stall[s] out their attacks' PP" against setup sweepers (Dragonite, Gliscor, Kingambit). Sole-remover caveat still applies: preserve pressure is a TEAM property this per-species file cannot express. PP-stalling matters in the long grinds where the stall audit measured real PP bankruptcy. [SCHEMA GAP, reviewer note: preserve also depends on whether OUR OWN team carries another remover — a team property this per-species file cannot express, and `conditional` only covers opponent facts. Moved out of the consumer-facing note 2026-07-31.]

sets.name: Defensive
sets.fact: Pressure makes opponents spend two PP per move, wearing down attackers across long games while Defog clears hazards. Item choice splits between Rocky Helmet, which punishes contact, and Leftovers for passive recovery; both play the same defensive role.
sets.prevalence_note: The only named set, so ~100% by construction rather than by measurement. Its real variation is item choice (Rocky Helmet or Leftovers) and ability (Pressure or Mirror Armor), neither of which changes the role.

rillaboom.fact: Grassy Surge sets Grassy Terrain, which heals every grounded Pokemon each turn and weakens Earthquake — a benefit to its whole side that ends when it does. Grassy Glide gains priority in terrain.
rillaboom.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Rillaboom (gen9ou) — Utility]: Grassy Terrain is described as "solving its problem with longevity" for partners and enabling Grassy-Seed setup — i.e. the terrain is a TEAM-WIDE annuity (passive recovery + halved Earthquake), not a personal buff, so the setter's death ends a resource the whole side was drawing on. Same economics shape as the weather setters; RE-RUN the rain_audit for terrain before assigning preserve pressure, since sun leaked identically to rain and did not care.

sets.name: Choice Band
sets.fact: Choice Band makes Grassy Glide a hard-hitting priority move under its own terrain.

sets.name: Utility
sets.fact: A support build that keeps terrain up and pivots with U-turn rather than attacking outright.

walkingwake.fact: Hydro Steam is strengthened rather than weakened in sun. Protosynthesis activates in sun or from Booster Energy, so it still functions when the sun is gone.
walkingwake.provenance: Hydro Steam is sun-boosted rather than sun-nerfed, and Protosynthesis falls back on Booster Energy when the sun drops — which is exactly WHY sun tolerates engine piloting (63%) while rain does not (29.2%, benched). Recorded to keep the weather fix from treating all abusers as equally weather-dependent.

dragonite.fact: Multiscale halves incoming damage only at full HP, so it needs an undamaged entry to function. Roost restores that condition. Dragon Dance turns one safe turn into a sweep.
dragonite.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Dragonite (gen9ou)]: Roost-based sets "give Dragonite easy setup opportunities" and let it check Ogerpon-W, Iron Moth and Rillaboom, "with Multiscale intact". Same entry_condition family as Ceruledge: Multiscale only halves damage at FULL HP, so entry chip deletes the defensive half of the wincon before it sets up — which is why the standard set runs Boots. The eval prices Multiscale when at full HP but cannot price PRESERVING full HP for a later sweep.
sequence: enter at FULL HP — Multiscale halves the incoming hit only from full, and Heavy-Duty Boots are what keep it full through hazards
Dragon Dance while Multiscale absorbs the first attack, raising Attack and Speed
sweep with Earthquake and its coverage move
Extreme Speed finishes anything faster or already weakened, ignoring Speed entirely
Roost when the sweep stalls: it restores full HP and with it Multiscale, buying another setup turn
dragonite.sequence_note: Roost is not only healing — returning to full HP restores the Multiscale damage halving, so it effectively refreshes the setup window. Chip damage that prevents reaching full HP removes that option permanently.

sets.name: Dragon Dance
sets.fact: Dragon Dance raises Attack and Speed behind Multiscale, then Extreme Speed cleans up.

sets.name: Bulky Phazer
sets.fact: Three attacks with Roost, using Multiscale and recovery to check threats rather than to set up.

sequence: enter at FULL HP on a free switch — Focus Sash only functions from full, so entry chip cancels the plan
Swords Dance while they attack or switch
TAKE the hit: Sash holds at 1 HP, which procs Weak Armor for +Speed (losing the Sash here is the mechanism, not a loss)
now outspeeding: attack with Bitter Blade, whose drain heals back off 1 HP
hold Shadow Sneak in reserve for anything that still outspeeds or carries priority
ceruledge.sequence_note: Every step scores badly on its own — 1 HP, no item, lowered Defense — and only the finished chain is a sweep. Judging any single turn of it in isolation rejects the plan.
ceruledge.fact: Weak Armor raises its Speed when it is hit. Bitter Blade heals it for half the damage dealt. Focus Sash survives one hit but only from full HP. Shadow Sneak provides priority. Most sets carry Weak Armor; a minority run Flash Fire instead, which grants a Fire immunity rather than a Speed boost when hit.
ceruledge.provenance: TWICE-CORRECTED, and the final read is the user's (2026-07-31). (1) My inference: 'Focus Sash is a resource chip destroys, so preserve it.' (2) RAG partly corrected it [smogon#Ceruledge (gen9ou) — Swords Dance]: popping the Sash with weak moves "would only give it a trouble-free Weak Armor boost", so the opponent removing the Sash is often GOOD for Ceruledge — I then over-corrected to preserve:low. (3) The real mechanism is a SEQUENCE, and entry chip is what breaks it: come in at FULL HP (Focus Sash only functions from full), Swords Dance, TAKE a hit, survive at 1 HP on Sash, which procs Weak Armor for +Speed, then outspeed and heal back with Bitter Blade's drain, holding Shadow Sneak in reserve for anything that still outspeeds or carries priority. So the Sash is not a thing to protect and not a thing to spend — it is the PIVOT of a multi-turn plan whose precondition is an uncontested entry. Any Stealth Rock chip kills the plan before turn one. DIRECTLY TIED to our pinned loss mechanism (SR = 21% of damage taken in the long grinds): this is a mon whose wincon the hazard war silently deletes, which is also why the standard set wants removal or Boots support. The whole sequence is exactly the beyond-horizon multi-turn plan the leaf eval cannot price. [Cross-references removed from the consumer-facing note 2026-07-31: it had pointed at Hatterene's bait-switch and the Curse/Dondozo accumulation. Those parallels are real and useful to a reviewer, but each entry must stand alone for a consumer.] [EXPANDED 2026-07-31 from full multi-angle retrieval: Smogon names TWO sets and I had only the Swords Dance one. The Bulk Up set is a different mon in practice — it boosts Defence rather than buying a turn with Focus Sash, carries Taunt to stop Defog, and wants screens rather than a clean entry. The sequence recorded on this entry is the Swords Dance line specifically.]

sets.name: Swords Dance
sets.fact: Swords Dance doubles Attack for a fast sweep, with Focus Sash surviving one hit from full HP so the boost can be taken.

sets.name: Bulk Up
sets.fact: A minority set. Bulk Up raises Attack and Defence together, so it boosts while absorbing physical hits rather than relying on Focus Sash, and Taunt on this set denies Defog. It appears mainly on hyper-offence and screens teams, where the extra turns make boosting practical.

ironmoth.fact: Booster Energy is spent on entry to raise its best stat. Fiery Dance can raise its Special Attack further, letting it sweep once boosted.
ironmoth.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Iron Moth (gen9ou) — Booster Energy]: the recommended set is Booster Energy with Fiery Dance / Sludge Wave / coverage / Substitute, i.e. the item is spent on entry BY DESIGN to switch on Quark Drive. Consistent with the item-polarity finding (consumption is the point, not a loss). Remaining unpriced question is TIMING — which entry spends it — which the eval does not model.

tinglu.fact: Vessel of Ruin weakens opposing Special Attack. It sets Stealth Rock and Spikes, and Whirlwind forces switches so those hazards keep applying.
tinglu.provenance: richwoman's most-used lead by a distance (45 of her games) and the anchor of the hazard-stack that produces our pinned chip loss. Her revealed set is SR/Whirlwind/Earthquake/Ruination — Whirlwind is what converts her hazards into forced-switch chip.

deoxysspeed.fact: Extreme Speed stat lets it set hazards or screens before almost anything else moves. Focus Sash guarantees it acts at least twice.
deoxysspeed.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Deoxys-Speed (gen9ou) — Hazard Lead]: "Focus Sash guarantees it can set at least one layer of entry hazard against faster threats... or even set two layers against slower threats" — the set is explicitly built to trade itself for hazards, confirming the suicide-lead role rather than a mon to preserve.

sets.name: Hazard Lead
sets.fact: Focus Sash guarantees it survives to set at least one layer before it falls.

sets.name: Nasty Plot
sets.fact: Nasty Plot turns its extreme Speed into a sweep instead of hazard support.

pecharunt.fact: Poison Puppeteer confuses any foe it poisons. Bulk and recovery let it stall and spread status.
pecharunt.provenance: CORRECTION 2026-07-31 (user-flagged, verified): Poison Puppeteer IS implemented — generate_instructions.rs:907 adds CONFUSION to a foe it poisons, landed in 2e000e6 alongside Rock Head/Anger Shell/Synchronize. An earlier memory note listing it as a silent OU gap was stale. The engine models it correctly; this is now an ordinary role entry.

sets.name: Nasty Plot
sets.fact: Nasty Plot turns it from a status spreader into an attacker behind its bulk.

sets.name: Pivot
sets.fact: Boots and recovery let it come in repeatedly to spread poison and confusion.

ironvaliant.fact: High mixed offense with Booster Energy spent on entry to raise its best stat. Choice Specs Moonblast breaks special walls that normally check it.
ironvaliant.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Iron Valiant (gen9ou)]: "Choice Specs takes advantage of Moonblast's spammability and lets Iron Valiant break through and even 2HKO otherwise common Iron Valiant answers such as Assault Vest Hatterene, Galarian Weezing, and specially defensive Gliscor." Booster Energy is its top item by usage — a one-shot entry resource like Iron Moth's, so entry TIMING is the unpriced question. [CORRECTED 2026-07-31: I had written a Swords Dance set. Usage says Calm Mind 7.6% against Swords Dance 3.9%, with Encore at 8.8% and Booster Energy on 80% of sets — the setup set is special, and Encore is the enabler.]

sets.name: Choice Specs
sets.fact: Choice Specs locks it into one move but lets Moonblast break special walls that would otherwise check it.

sets.name: Calm Mind
sets.fact: Calm Mind raises Special Attack and Special Defense together, and Encore can manufacture the free turn to use it.
sequence: enter on something passive — Booster Energy activates on entry and raises its highest stat
Encore locks the opponent into a move that cannot threaten it, creating a guaranteed free turn
Calm Mind while they are locked, raising Special Attack and Special Defense
sweep with Moonblast and its coverage move once the boost is up
sets.sequence_note: Encore is what makes the setup safe rather than hopeful: without it the free turn has to be predicted, and its frailty means a wrong read ends the attempt immediately.

sets.name: Swords Dance
sets.fact: Swords Dance doubles Attack for a physical sweep, with Close Combat and Knock Off as coverage.

sets.name: Mixed
sets.fact: Booster Energy on entry with both physical and special attacks, so no single wall answers it.

ragingbolt.fact: Thunderclap is a priority move, so it revenge-kills faster threats and beats slower priority attackers. Its value is largely in being held back until something needs killing.
ragingbolt.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Raging Bolt (gen9ou) — Choice Specs]: "Thunderclap is used as powerful priority to revenge kill or force out faster threats such as Ogerpon-W, Iron Valiant, and Enamorus, and it also helps Raging Bolt beat slower priority users such as Kingambit and Scizor." Priority-in-reserve is a role the leaf eval sees only as a weak move until the turn it matters — same shape as Ceruledge's Shadow Sneak.

sets.name: Choice Specs
sets.fact: Choice Specs locks it in but makes Draco Meteor and Thunderclap break through immediately.

sets.name: Boots Pivot
sets.fact: Boots let it re-enter through hazards while Thunderclap threatens priority every time.

zamazenta.fact: Dauntless Shield raises its Defense on entry. Bulk and typing let it check many physical attackers, so teams are often built expecting it to hold that job all game.
zamazenta.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Zamazenta (gen9ou)]: "Zamazenta is the tier's most consistent glue piece and wincon. Its natural bulk alongside a valuable typing, which can be boosted further by Dauntless Shield, lets it take on many manner of offensive threats like Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, some Dragonite sets, and Great Tusk." Glue = it is what other members are built around; losing it costs more than its own HP.

sets.name: IronPress
sets.fact: Iron Defense with Body Press turns its Defence into offence, a win condition that needs several turns.

sets.name: Offensive Attacker
sets.fact: Four attacks using its Speed and typing to threaten immediately instead of setting up.

ogerponwellspring.fact: Water Absorb heals it whenever it is hit by a Water move, so it can enter freely on one. Ivy Cudgel is its signature move and becomes Water-type while it holds the Wellspring Mask, with a raised critical-hit rate. It runs one Grass move alongside it rather than both — usually Horn Leech, which drains HP back, sometimes Power Whip for raw power. Swords Dance doubles its Attack, and Trailblaze can be run to raise its Speed by one stage when it hits.
ogerponwellspring.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Ogerpon-Wellspring (gen9ou)]: "one of OU's premier physical attackers" with "the high power of Ivy Cudgel and Power Whip, the option to trade the latter with Trailblaze to outspeed otherwise faster foes". Trailblaze makes it a conditional sweeper — a setup curve the eval prices only one turn at a time. [USER-CORRECTED 2026-07-31: my fact implied it runs Ivy Cudgel AND Power Whip together. It picks ONE Grass move — usage confirms Ivy Cudgel 24.9% (on essentially every set, since four moves cap at 25%), with the Grass slot split between Horn Leech 10.3% and Power Whip 5.8%, so Horn Leech is the commoner choice and I had named the rarer one. Swords Dance 15.1%. Trailblaze does not reach the top eight, consistent with it being an option rather than standard. The play sequence was missing entirely.] [EXPANDED 2026-07-31: three named sets, not one. The sequence on this entry is the Swords Dance line; the All-Out Attacker and Utility sets do not set up at all.]
sequence: enter on something it walls — a Water move heals it outright through Water Absorb
Swords Dance while the opponent switches or attacks into its bulk
optionally click Trailblaze first, trading a turn of damage for +1 Speed when outspeeding is what is missing
sweep with Ivy Cudgel and its single Grass move, Horn Leech draining HP back as it goes
ogerponwellspring.sequence_note: The Speed boost is a choice, not a given: it is worth a turn only when something relevant would otherwise move first. Setting up costs a turn either way, so the entry has to be genuinely free.

sets.name: Swords Dance
sets.fact: Swords Dance doubles Attack, with Trailblaze optionally traded in for a Speed boost when outspeeding is what is missing.

sets.name: All-Out Attacker
sets.fact: Four attacks and no setup, hitting immediately on entry rather than asking for a free turn.
sets.prevalence_note: No positive signature — this set is defined by what it LACKS (no setup move, or an item every set carries), so its share is estimated as whatever the signature-derived sets leave over. Less reliable than a signature estimate: it absorbs their combined error, and the sets may not partition cleanly.

sets.name: Utility
sets.fact: Knock Off, U-turn and Encore trade damage for disruption and momentum instead of setting up.

dragapult.fact: Infiltrator ignores Substitutes and screens. Very high Speed with U-turn makes it a momentum pivot rather than a mon to hold back. Roughly a third of sets run Clear Body instead of Infiltrator, trading the ability to bypass Substitutes and screens for immunity to stat drops.
dragapult.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Dragapult (gen9ou) — Boots Pivot]: "Infiltrator is the preferred ability, as it allows Dragapult to both hit and cripple foes regardless of" substitutes and screens. Infiltrator ignoring Substitute/screens is a matchup fact the eval does model; the role note is that it is the momentum piece, not a mon to hold back.

sets.name: Choice Specs
sets.fact: Choice Specs locks it in but lets Draco Meteor and Shadow Ball break through immediately.

sets.name: Boots Pivot
sets.fact: Heavy-Duty Boots plus U-turn make it a repeated-entry momentum pivot.

conditional.note: Magic Bounce only does something if the opponent actually carries hazard or status moves to reflect. Against a team that sets hazards it is the reason those hazards never land; against one that does not, it is an ordinary bulky attacker.
conditional.usage: It is switched in on a turn the setter is expected to act, so the hazard move is reflected back onto them. Inviting that attempt is the point, so only bringing it in when it is safe never collects the value.

hatterene.fact: Magic Bounce reflects hazards and status back at the user, so it PREVENTS hazards rather than removing them — it must be in play when the setter acts. Healing Wish trades it away to fully restore a teammate.
hatterene.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Hatterene (gen9ou) — Healing Wish]: Magic Bounce denies hazards passively while alive; "Psychic Noise notably lets Hatterene significantly chip bulky foes like Gliscor, Garganacl, and Clefable, preventing them from recovering their health", and the Healing Wish set trades itself to "pivot them in safely". TWO team-persistent effects the eval cannot price: (a) Magic Bounce is hazard PREVENTION, worth most against exactly the hazard-stack that beats us — its death re-opens the SR war; (b) Healing Wish is a deliberate SACRIFICE that restores a teammate, so a low-HP Hatterene is not obviously a liability. Psychic Noise blocking recovery also matters in the long grinds where the recovery war is even. CONDITIONAL + DEPLOYMENT added 2026-07-31 (user): the static schema could not express that Magic Bounce's worth depends on the OPPONENT's roster, nor that the mon is played as a setup-baiting switch-in rather than a lead.

sets.name: Healing Wish
sets.fact: Healing Wish trades it away to restore a teammate to full HP and clear their status.

sets.name: Calm Mind
sets.fact: Calm Mind raises both special stats behind Magic Bounce, turning it into a win condition.

sets.name: Pain Split
sets.fact: Pain Split averages HP with the target, giving it recovery it otherwise lacks.

irontreads.fact: Rapid Spin removes hazards and Stealth Rock sets them, so it can do either job. Quark Drive raises a stat on entry.
irontreads.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Iron Treads (gen9ou) — Lead]: The Lead set trades itself for hazard control and "gives it another way to block Defog and Rapid Spin"; coverage choice is explicitly about stopping Raging Bolt boosting or "Pecharunt from blocking Rapid Spin". Dual hazard role (sets AND removes) makes it a lead by design rather than a mon to preserve.

sets.name: Lead
sets.fact: Booster Energy makes it fast enough to set or remove hazards before most leads act.

sets.name: Utility
sets.fact: Leftovers and bulk let it keep removing hazards across the game rather than once.

kyurem.fact: High mixed offense across several very different sets, so which set it is changes what counters it. Freeze-Dry hits Water types super effectively.
kyurem.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Kyurem (gen9ou)]: "one of SV OU's strongest offensive Pokemon, utilizing its powerful mixed offensive stats and solid overall bulk to run a wide variety of sets, each requiring different counterplay. Choice Specs makes Kyurem into a wallbreaker." 'Each set requires different counterplay' is a direct statement that set inference matters more than usual here — relevant to the belief-tier work. [Split into sets 2026-07-31: its own analysis says each set 'requires different counterplay', so a single species role is misleading here.] [CORRECTED 2026-07-31: I had written a 'Substitute Roost' set, but Roost does not appear in its moves at all. Usage: Choice Specs 25% / Loaded Dice 23% / Leftovers 23% items; Dragon Dance 6.7% with Icicle Spear 7.0% and Scale Shot 4.7% is the Loaded Dice physical set; Substitute 6.6% with Protect 3.4% is the stall set.]

sets.name: Choice Specs
sets.fact: Choice Specs locks it into one move but lets Freeze-Dry and Earth Power break walls outright. Freeze-Dry hits Water types super effectively.

sets.name: Dragon Dance (Loaded Dice)
sets.fact: Dragon Dance raises Attack and Speed, and Loaded Dice makes Icicle Spear and Scale Shot hit four or five times reliably.
sequence: enter on a hit it resists or a forced switch
Dragon Dance, raising Attack and Speed together
Icicle Spear with Loaded Dice, which guarantees four or five hits and so breaks Substitutes and Focus Sash
Scale Shot when more Speed is needed — it raises Speed but lowers Defense, so it commits to winning quickly

sets.name: Substitute
sets.fact: Substitute on a predicted switch blocks status and chip, and Protect with Leftovers stalls further while Freeze-Dry and Earth Power attack from behind it.

conditional.note: Ceaseless Edge sets Spikes as part of an attack, so it still lays hazards against opponents carrying Magic Bounce or Taunt, which stop moves like Stealth Rock and Spikes.

samurotthisui.fact: Ceaseless Edge sets Spikes as part of an attack, so it lays hazards even through Magic Bounce and Taunt, which stop ordinary setters. Sharpness boosts its cutting moves.
samurotthisui.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Samurott-Hisui (gen9ou)]: "one of the most prolific entry hazard setters in the tier with its signature move Ceaseless Edge, letting it both set Spikes and deal heavy damage thanks to its Sharpness ability. It can even do so in the face of Hatterene's Magic Bounce and Taunt." Setting hazards THROUGH Magic Bounce is the counter to hazard-denial — the other side of the war that decides our long games.

sets.name: Lead
sets.fact: Focus Sash guarantees it survives to set Spikes with Ceaseless Edge.

sets.name: Choice Scarf
sets.fact: A Choice Scarf lets it revenge-kill while still setting Spikes through Ceaseless Edge.

sets.name: Assault Vest
sets.fact: Assault Vest adds special bulk so it can keep setting Spikes across the game.

cinderace.fact: Court Change swaps all side conditions, moving hazards onto the opponent instead of clearing them. Libero changes its type to match the move it uses, and U-turn pivots. Roughly a third of sets run Blaze instead of Libero, keeping a fixed Fire typing.
cinderace.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Cinderace (gen9ou) — Offensive Pivot]: Recommended set is "Pyro Ball; U-turn; Court Change; ..." with Heavy-Duty Boots and Libero. COURT CHANGE is hazard control by THEFT — it flips our hazards onto them rather than clearing them, which is strictly better in a chip war and is why our ah3 team runs it. The eval sees a side-condition swap but not that it converts their investment into ours.

sets.name: Offensive Pivot
sets.fact: Heavy-Duty Boots with Pyro Ball, U-turn and Court Change, pivoting freely through hazards while moving them onto the opponent.

sets.name: Choice Band
sets.fact: A Choice Band build that locks in for immediate power, still able to U-turn out of a bad lock.

landorustherian.fact: Intimidate lowers the opposing Attack every time it enters, so repeated switch-ins compound the effect. U-turn pivots; Earthquake and Stealth Rock add utility.
landorustherian.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Landorus-Therian (gen9ou)]: "one of OU's premier pivots. It can check a wide variety of threats such as Kingambit, Ceruledge, and Raging Bolt." Intimidate is a persistent team-wide defensive effect applied on every entry — an annuity the eval prices only as a one-off stat drop.

sets.name: Defensive
sets.fact: Rocky Helmet punishes contact while Intimidate and bulk let it check physical attackers repeatedly.

sets.name: Offensive
sets.fact: A Choice Scarf turns it into a revenge killer that still pivots with U-turn.

alomomola.fact: Regenerator restores HP on switch out and Wish heals a teammate, so it is a healing source for the whole side rather than only itself. Flip Turn pivots.
alomomola.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Alomomola (gen9ou) — WishFish (Wish Passer)]: Recommended set is "Flip Turn; Wish; Protect; Scald / Tickle" with Regenerator. TEAM-WIDE HEALING ANNUITY: Wish heals a TEAMMATE, and Regenerator heals itself on every switch — so its survival is a recurring income stream for the whole side, the same economics as Poison Heal Gliscor. Directly relevant to the recovery war measured in the long grinds.

sets.name: WishFish
sets.fact: Wish heals a teammate and Flip Turn pivots out, so its bulk is spent supporting the side rather than itself.

sets.name: Assault Vest
sets.fact: Assault Vest trades its status moves for special bulk, so it walls attackers but can no longer pass Wish.

darkrai.fact: Very high Speed, usually with Choice Scarf, makes it a revenge killer. Trick hands the Choice item to a wall to cripple it.
darkrai.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Darkrai (gen9ou) — Choice Scarf]: "Darkrai can also cripple physical walls like Dondozo and Skarmory with Trick." Trick converts its own item into a liability on their wall — a resource TRADE the eval scores as an item swap. Also the species our speed-floor inference must not mistake for a Scarf when it is not (see the 88f1f17 correction).

sets.name: Nasty Plot
sets.fact: Nasty Plot doubles Special Attack for a sweep once its checks are gone.

sets.name: Choice Specs
sets.fact: Choice Specs locks it into one move but breaks walls immediately on entry.

sets.name: Boots Attacker
sets.fact: Heavy-Duty Boots let it re-enter through hazards repeatedly while holding four attacks.

zapdos.fact: Volt Switch pivots while Roost restores HP, so it re-enters many times a game. Heavy-Duty Boots let it ignore entry hazards while doing so.
zapdos.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Zapdos (gen9ou) — Offensive]: Recommended set "Hurricane; Volt Switch; Heat Wave; Roost" with Heavy-Duty Boots: "a very proactive Pokemon that can help gain momentum." Boots + Roost = a mon designed to re-enter repeatedly, so its value is in the switch economy the hazard war taxes.

sets.name: Defensive
sets.fact: Roost with bulk lets it check physical attackers repeatedly and pivot with Volt Switch.

sets.name: Offensive
sets.fact: Hurricane and Heat Wave threaten damage while Volt Switch keeps momentum.

garganacl.fact: Purifying Salt blocks status. Iron Defense with Body Press converts its Defense into attacking power, while Salt Cure chips and Recover sustains — a slow plan that needs several turns to pay off.
garganacl.provenance: RAG-grounded [smogon#Garganacl (gen9ou) — Iron Defense]: "With fantastic bulk, Salt Cure, Purifying Salt's status immunity, the combination of Iron Defense" and Body Press + Recover. IronPress is a slow multi-turn wincon whose intermediate states look flat — the exact accumulation pattern the leaf eval prunes (the documented Curse/Dondozo failure mode). Salt Cure is chip we measured at only 1% of damage taken, so its threat here is the setup, not the chip.
sequence: enter on a physical attacker it walls — Purifying Salt blocks any status they try to stick on it
Iron Defense, and keep using it while Recover undoes the chip they deal
Body Press attacks using the boosted Defense stat, so every Iron Defense raises its damage too
Salt Cure anything that switches in, chipping it every turn it stays
garganacl.sequence_note: This is a slow plan that needs several uninterrupted turns, and each early turn looks like it accomplishes nothing — the payoff only exists once Defense is high enough that Body Press threatens. Anything that forces it out resets the whole attempt.

sets.name: Iron Defense
sets.fact: Iron Defense with Body Press converts Defence into attacking power over several turns.

sets.name: Curse
sets.fact: Curse trades Speed for Attack and Defence, a slower but self-sufficient win condition.

sets.name: Stealth Rock
sets.fact: A support build that sets Stealth Rock and chips with Salt Cure instead of setting up.
